Screen content always comes from the raw stream. So if the board shows 10 done, the notices were in the stream. A notice could be split by interleaved escapes (hence the number-prefix matching), but the set-based assertion handles that (already in place).

# frozen_string_literal: true

# Play listing-image sync (issue #947). Plain ruby, no gems — the same
# contract as play_upload_preflight.rb so the CI fastlane suites run it on
# the runner's stock ruby.
#
# Why this exists: the supply `play_store` lane only UPLOADS images. Play
# appends screenshot uploads to the existing set, so whatever is stale on
# the listing (an old-copy screenshot, a device type or locale the repo no
# longer generates — ru-RU tenInch, for instance) survives the upload
# forever. Google reviewed that stale image and rejected the dev.fa1.app
# update on Sep 24 while the repo goldens were already fixed.
#
# This module replaces the WHOLE listing-image state per locale and device
# type, then proves the committed state matches the repo goldens:
#
#   1. one edit: clear every managed screenshot set for EVERY listing
#      locale (repo locales ∪ locales live on the Play listing), then
#      upload the committed goldens (sorted — file name order is the
#      listing order), checking each stored sha256 against the local file
#      (gh-1328: a nil stored sha means Play is still processing — the
#      read is retried with backoff, and an unreadable remote aborts with
#      its own "remote unreadable" class, never as a byte mismatch);
#   2. commit — a failed upload aborts BEFORE the commit, so the live
#      listing keeps its previous state;
#   3. a fresh read-only edit re-reads edits.images.list and fails the job
#      unless every managed locale/type matches the goldens exactly
#      (icon + featureGraphic + all screenshot types, empty where the repo
#      ships nothing).
#
# supply keeps handling the metadata TEXTS (the lane passes
# skip_upload_images/skip_upload_screenshots); images ride this module only.
require "base64"
require "digest"
require "json"
require "net/http"
require "openssl"
require "uri"

module PlayListingSync
  API_ROOT = "https://androidpublisher.googleapis.com/androidpublisher/v3/applications"
  # Media-upload host prefix: edits.images.upload POSTs the SAME path under
  # the /upload/ prefix with ?uploadType=media (gh-1261).
  UPLOAD_ROOT = "https://androidpublisher.googleapis.com/upload/androidpublisher/v3/applications"
  TOKEN_URL = "https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token"
  SCOPE = "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/androidpublisher"

  # Multi-slot types: Play APPENDS uploads, so every listing locale gets its
  # remote set cleared first — including types the repo no longer generates
  # (ru-RU tenInchScreenshots) and never generated (sevenInchScreenshots).
  SCREENSHOT_TYPES = %w[phoneScreenshots sevenInchScreenshots tenInchScreenshots].freeze
  # Single-slot types: an upload replaces the stored image by itself.
  SINGLE_IMAGE_TYPES = %w[icon featureGraphic].freeze
  # The image types this sync manages. validate_image_type! pins every
  # image call against this list BEFORE any HTTP request — it is a
  # module-local guard, NOT the full AppImageType enum (tvScreenshots,
  # wearScreenshots, promo graphics, …). EXTEND THIS LIST (in lock-step
  # with clear_plan/expected_state/sync_and_verify!) when adding managed
  # types, or the new types will be rejected pre-flight.
  MANAGED_TYPES = (SCREENSHOT_TYPES + SINGLE_IMAGE_TYPES).freeze

  module_function

  # ── pure helpers (unit-tested, no I/O beyond the metadata dir) ──────────

  # The locale dirs the repo ships (fastlane/metadata/android/<locale>/).
  def repo_locales(metadata_dir)
    Dir.children(metadata_dir)
       .select { |entry| File.directory?(File.join(metadata_dir, entry)) }
       .sort
  end

  # Committed golden paths for a locale/type, sorted (file name order IS
  # the Play listing order). Screenshot types live in an images/<type>/
  # dir; the single-slot types are flat files (images/icon.png,
  # images/featureGraphic.png). Missing everything = the repo ships none.
  def local_images(metadata_dir, locale, type)
    dir = File.join(metadata_dir, locale, "images", type)
    file = "#{dir}.png"
    paths =
      if Dir.exist?(dir)
        Dir.children(dir).grep(/\.png\z/i).sort.map { |name| File.join(dir, name) }
      elsif File.exist?(file)
        [file]
      else
        []
      end
    paths.sort
  end

  def sha256(path)
    Digest::SHA256.file(path).hexdigest
  end

  # The screenshot sets to clear: every listing locale (repo ∪ live on the
  # console) × every multi-slot type.
  def clear_plan(metadata_dir, remote_locales)
    all_locales(metadata_dir, remote_locales).flat_map do |locale|
      SCREENSHOT_TYPES.map { |type| { locale: locale, type: type } }
    end
  end

  # The post-sync state the listing must have: sha256 SEQUENCES per
  # [locale, type] in listing order (local_images sorts — file name order
  # IS the Play listing order) — the repo goldens where they exist, empty
  # where they do not (ru-RU tenInch, dropped locales).
  #
  # icon/featureGraphic are single-slot brand assets and Play Console does
  # not allow an empty icon on a listing locale, so for locales the repo
  # does NOT ship they are "don't care": a console-created locale keeps
  # its icon/feature graphic (the sync only clears + enforces the
  # screenshot sets there — issue #947 review).
  def expected_state(metadata_dir, remote_locales)
    repo = repo_locales(metadata_dir)
    all_locales(metadata_dir, remote_locales).to_h do |locale|
      types = repo.include?(locale) ? MANAGED_TYPES : SCREENSHOT_TYPES
      [locale, types.to_h { |type|
        [type, local_images(metadata_dir, locale, type).map { |path| sha256(path) }]
      }]
    end
  end

  def all_locales(metadata_dir, remote_locales)
    (repo_locales(metadata_dir) + remote_locales.to_a).uniq.sort
  end

# frozen_string_literal: true

# Issue #947 — Play listing-image sync. Plain ruby, no gems (runs on the
# CI runner's stock ruby), mirroring play_upload_preflight_test.rb:
#
#   ruby flutter_app/fastlane/test/play_listing_sync_test.rb
#
# Everything is exercised against a stateful fake of the androidpublisher
# REST transport — no network. The fake records every call so the checks
# pin the exact behaviour the Sep 24 rejection demanded: stale screenshot
# sets deleted per locale + device type (including ru-RU tenInch and
# never-generated sevenInch), goldens uploaded with sha256 verification,
# commit only after every image checks out, and a post-commit
# edits.images.list gate that fails on any drift.
#
# Guarded by $PROGRAM_NAME so an accidental require by fastlane's loader
# never executes the checks.

require "digest"
require "json"
require "openssl"
require "tmpdir"
require "fileutils"

require_relative "../play_listing_sync"

if $PROGRAM_NAME == __FILE__
  $checks = 0

  def ok(message)
    $checks += 1
    puts "  ok #{message}"
  end

  # ── fake transport ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Stateful androidpublisher stand-in: token → edit → listings →
  # delete/upload/list images → commit/delete-edit. The image paths mirror
  # the REAL androidpublisher v3 contract (gh-1261): the AppImageType enum
  # value sits DIRECTLY in the path (.../listings/<locale>/<imageType>) —
  # there is no "images" collection segment.
  class FakePlayHttp
    attr_reader :calls, :store, :committed
    attr_accessor :upload_sha_override, :upload_omit_sha, :token_response, :remote_languages,
                  :post_commit_drift, :post_commit_reverse, :image_delete_error,
                  :edit_insert_error, :listings_error, :commit_error,
                  :hide_shas_until_list_no

    def initialize
      @calls = []
      @store = Hash.new { |h, key| h[key] = [] }
      @committed = []
      @remote_languages = %w[en-US ru-RU]
      @list_reads = Hash.new(0)
    end

    def request(method, url, headers: {}, body: nil, content_type: nil)
      @calls << [method, url]
      case
      when method == :Post && url.include?("oauth2.googleapis.com/token")
        @token_assertion = body
        @token_response || { status: 200, body: { access_token: "[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]" }.to_json }
      when method == :Post && url.end_with?("/edits")
        return @edit_insert_error if @edit_insert_error
        { status: 200, body: { id: "edit1" }.to_json }
      when method == :Get && url.end_with?("/listings")
        return @listings_error if @listings_error
        { status: 200, body: { listings: @remote_languages.map { |l| { language: l } } }.to_json }
      when method == :Delete && (m = url.match(%r{/listings/([^/]+)/([^/]+)\z}))
        return @image_delete_error if @image_delete_error
        @store.delete([m[1], m[2]])
        { status: 204, body: "" }
      when method == :Post && (m = url.match(%r{/listings/([^/]+)/([^/]+)\?uploadType=media\z}))
        sha = @upload_sha_override || Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(body.to_s)
        @store[[m[1], m[2]]] << sha
        # gh-1328: Play sometimes 200s the upload WITHOUT a usable sha256
        # while the image is still processing.
        { status: 200, body: (@upload_omit_sha ? {} : { sha256: sha }).to_json }
      when method == :Get && (m = url.match(%r{/listings/([^/]+)/([^/]+)\z}))
        key = [m[1], m[2]]
        @list_reads[key] += 1
        images = @store[key].map { |s| { sha256: s } }
        # Post-commit drift injection: the committed listing keeps an image
        # the sync never uploaded (the stale-state failure mode #947 gates).
        if !@committed.empty? && @post_commit_drift == key

        # image set in a different order (the ordering failure mode).

        # finishes processing the just-uploaded bytes.
        images = images.map { |img| { sha256: nil } } if @hide_shas_until_list_no && @list_reads[key] <= @hide_shas_until_list_no

**Finding 1 (Thread 1 — empty-string sha)**: The gate `if stored.nil?` misses `""`. RED test: script an upload whose body is `{"sha256": ""}`. Currently FakePlayHttp's `upload_sha_override` returns `{ status: 200, body: { sha256: "" }.to_json }`... wait: `sha = @upload_sha_override || Digest...` — if override is `""`, `"" || x` → `""` is truthy in ruby (only nil/false are falsy), so sha = "". Then `@store << ""` and body `{ sha256: "" }`. Then in sync_and_verify!, `stored = ""`. `stored.nil?` → false → falls to `unless stored == local` → raises `remote sha mismatch ... (sha256 "" != local ...)`. RED confirmed by reasoning; the new test should assert that an empty-string upload sha routes to the poll (unreadable) path — with the listing materializing → green; or never materializing → `remote unreadable` class, NOT `remote sha mismatch` / `stored different bytes`.

Implementation: change `if stored.nil?` → `if stored.to_s.strip.empty?`. Then `poll_stored_sha!` gets `verified_prefix + [local]`. Also — should the message "Play never returned a usable sha256" stay accurate? Yes.

But wait — there's a subtlety in `poll_stored_sha!`'s list-read side: `readable = ...map { |image| image["sha256"] }.compact` — compact drops nils but not `""`. An entry with `sha256: ""` in the LIST would be "readable garbage" → `readable.any? { |sha| !expected_prefix.include?(sha) }` → mismatch! For consistency with thread 1's spirit (".compact on the list-read side" — the thread cites the existing `.compact`), I should also reject empty strings on the list-read side: `.map { |image| image["sha256"] }.reject { |sha| sha.to_s.strip.empty? }`. But the same payload-shape argument applies to the list side: a `""` in the list during processing would classify as a false mismatch. Hmm wait, careful — do NOT over-expand. The thread asks for the upload gate only. But the list-side `""` is exactly the same class of false mismatch... **Finding 2 (Thread 2 — single-slot assumption doc)**: comment-only in the gh-1328 comment block at the top of the module and/or at `poll_stored_sha!`. Note: multi-slot sets are cleared first, so during processing the list can only hold missing/nil entries. Single-slot types (icon/featureGraphic) are NOT cleared — if Play served the OLD sha during processing instead of nil, `poll_stored_sha!` would classify `remote sha mismatch`. Document this assumption. Where? The docstring of poll_stored_sha! and/or the caller. I'll add to the poll_stored_sha! doc block.

**Finding 3 (Thread 3 — comment math)**: "(attempts × backoff seconds)" → "((attempts - 1) sleeps of `backoff` between `attempts` reads)". One-line comment fix in poll_stored_sha! docstring.

RED-first? This is a test-only pin of EXISTING deliberate behavior — it should be GREEN immediately (the branch already behaves that way). The 10th notice must be in the raw buffer before/when the board can show `10 done`. So anchoring on the drained row guarantees the harvest completeness. Confirmed: the Fastfile call site uses defaults. Now let me start the TDD work.

## Plan

**Fix 1 — CI root cause (BLOCKING): flaky PTY countdown drain** (`test/integration/shell_job_countdown_pty_test.dart`)
- RED evidence: CI run 37555363161 harvested {1..8} of 10; same family as gh-1250 (run 37521987367, {1..5} of 10).
- Fix: anchor the drained harvest on the drained board row (gh-1250 precedent commit a2e4bfabf), test-only.

**Fix 2 — Thread 1: empty-string sha hardening** (`play_listing_sync.rb`)
- RED: new unit — upload answers `{sha256: ""}` → must poll → never `remote sha mismatch`; plus list-side `""` entries treated as unreadable.
- GREEN: `stored.to_s.strip.empty?` gate + list-read `.reject { |sha| sha.to_s.strip.empty? }`.

**Fix 3 — Thread 2: single-slot assumption documented** (comment only).

**Fix 4 — Thread 3: comment math** (comment only).

**Fix 5 — Thread 4: partial-out-of-order pin** (test only, pins existing conservative behavior — green on arrival).

Then run: ruby suite full; dart countdown test + reg guard; write outputs.

Order of operations per TDD: write the RED tests first, run them against the unfixed module, then fix, then run everything.

Let me write the RED tests for thread 1 first. In the test file, after the existing "nil stored sha is retried" block, add:

```ruby
# gh-1328 rework: an EMPTY-STRING sha is the same unreadable payload shape —
# `{"sha256": ""}` must route to the poll, never to the byte-mismatch class.
poll = PollHttp.new([[{ "sha256" => "" }],
                     [{ "sha256" => sha1 }]])
verified = PlayListingSync.poll_stored_sha!(...)
```

Hmm wait — the poll unit drives poll_stored_sha! directly; the empty-string gate lives in sync_and_verify!'s caller side. To RED-test the gate, drive sync_and_verify! end-to-end with a FakePlayHttp whose upload returns `{sha256: ""}` and whose list materializes later:

```ruby
# End-to-end: `{"sha256": ""}` from the upload is the same UNREADABLE
# payload shape as an omitted field — it must poll to a verdict, never
# reach the byte-mismatch class (gh-1328 rework: thread-1 hardening).
Dir.mktmpdir do |root|
  http = FakePlayHttp.new
  http.upload_sha_override = ""   # {"sha256": ""} — truthy key, unusable sha
  http.hide_shas_until_list_no = 1
  metadata_dir = metadata_dir_with_goldens(root)
  summary = PlayListingSync.sync_and_verify!(...)
  # must go green, not raise remote sha mismatch
end
```

Wait — careful with `upload_sha_override = ""`: `sha = @upload_sha_override || Digest...` — "" is truthy in ruby → sha = "". Then `@store[key] << ""` — the store now holds "" as the stored sha! Then the list read returns `[{sha256: ""}]` — with `hide_shas_until_list_no = 1`, the first read of each key maps everything to `{sha256: nil}`... but the poll's compact drops nil → readable=[] → retry; on read 2, entries serve their stored shas = "" → readable = [""] → `readable.any? { |sha| !expected_prefix.include?(sha) }` → "" not in expected → FALSE MISMATCH again via the list side! This confirms the list side ALSO needs the emptiness reject for the end-to-end to go green.

So with both fixes:
- upload gate: `stored.to_s.strip.empty?` → poll.
- poll list-read: `.map { sha256 }.reject { |s| s.to_s.strip.empty? }` — hmm wait, but then readable = [] on read 2 too (entry sha is ""). read 2..N always [] → never equals expected → returns nil → raise `remote unreadable after 5 attempts`. So end-to-end with override "" → unreadable abort (not mismatch). That's the honest classification: the fake stored "" as the actual sha, Play served "" consistently — genuinely unreadable.

For a GREEN end-to-end variant: upload `""` but the STORED sha is fine — that's contradictory (the fake stores what it returns). Better green case: upload omit-sha (nil) as today → green (already covered). For the empty-string case the correct expected behavior is: poll → unreadable class, never mismatch. So the end-to-end test asserts the `remote unreadable after N attempts` raise, message NOT containing "stored different bytes", no commit. And optionally, if the listing later materializes with the REAL sha — impossible in this fake since it stored "". Fine: pin the classification.

Also a poll-level unit for list-side "": readable [""] with expected [sha1] → must be treated as unreadable (retry → nil), not mismatch:

```ruby
poll = PollHttp.new([[{ "sha256" => "" }]] * 2)
verdict = poll_stored_sha!(... expected [sha1] ...) → nil (not raise)
```

RED on both today: today the upload "" never reaches poll (gate nil-only) → e2e raises `remote sha mismatch (sha256 "" != local …)` → test red. The poll-level "" test: readable [""] → `any?{!include?}` → mismatch raise → test red. 

Now the partial-out-of-order pin (thread 4) — green on arrival.

Message wording: the caller's unreadable raise says "Play never returned a usable sha256 for the just-uploaded image" — thread 4's nano-nit says slightly off for the partial case but "not worth chasing" — leave.

Also should the upload-gate change update the module header comment? The header says "a nil stored sha means Play is still processing" — extend to "a nil/empty stored sha". Cheap and accurate.

Now the comment fixes:

Thread 3: in poll_stored_sha! docstring: "(attempts × backoff seconds)" → "((attempts - 1) sleeps of `backoff` between `attempts` reads)".

Thread 2: add to poll_stored_sha! docstring (and/or the gh-1328 caller comment): the single-slot assumption — for icon/featureGraphic replaces, no clear runs first, so during the processing window the listing is expected to serve a nil entry (or the old sha is gone once replacement lands); if Play ever serves the PREVIOUS image's sha for a single-slot replace, the poll classifies a mismatch — deliberate per the issue's foreign-sha→mismatch table. Document.

      final drained = await harness.waitForOutput(

```

And add the `_drainedRow` const, and use it in the final contains assertion (replacing the literal).

The final block currently:
```dart

```

{"newText":"  # gh-1328: edits.images.upload may answer 200 WITHOUT a usable sha256
  # (an omitted field → nil, or a blank string) while Play is still
  # processing the image. An unreadable sha is UNREADABLE, never a byte
  # mismatch — poll edits.images.list across the processing window
  # ((attempts - 1) sleeps of `backoff` between `attempts` reads) and only
  # then classify:
  #   returns the verified sha of the just-uploaded image once the readable
  #   set equals the goldens uploaded so far;
  #   raises "remote sha mismatch" on readable bytes contradicting the
  #   goldens (a real byte/ordering mismatch);
  #   returns nil when still unreadable after `attempts` — the caller
  #   aborts with the distinct "remote unreadable" class.
  #
  # Assumption (gh-1328 review): multi-slot sets are cleared first, so
  # during the processing window their list can only hold missing entries
  # or nil/blank shas — both retry. Single-slot types (icon/featureGraphic)
  # are NOT cleared (console-only locales keep theirs), so the poll relies
  # on Play serving a nil/blank entry — not the PREVIOUS image's sha —
  # while a replacement processes. A readable set contradicting the goldens
  # still classifies "remote sha mismatch" by design (the issue's
  # foreign-sha → mismatch table); if a daily leg ever reds on a single-slot
  # replace serving the old sha, treat that as unreadable here.
  def poll_stored_sha!(http, package_name, edit_id, locale, type, expected_prefix, auth,
                       attempts: 5, backoff: 30)
    attempts.times do |attempt|
      readable = list_images!(http, package_name, edit_id, locale, type, auth)
                 .map { |image| image["sha256"] }.reject { |sha| sha.to_s.strip.empty? }","oldText":"  # gh-1328: edits.images.upload may answer 200 WITHOUT a usable sha256

messages.preview: The failing test uses `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500)` to await the drain — but settle notices arrive ~1 s apart **by design** (staggered sleeps 3–12 s), so any CI jitter stretching one gap past the ~1 …

blocks.text:
I see the bug pattern now. In `waitForOutput`:

```dart
while (DateTime.now().isBefore(deadline)) {
  await Future<void>.delayed(Duration(milliseconds: settleMs));
  if (_rawBuffer.length == lastLength) {
    if (++stableTurns >= 2) break;
  } else {
    ...
  }
```

`waitForOutput` returns as soon as the raw buffer is stable for 2 consecutive settles (500 ms each in the drained call = ~1 s of silence). It does NOT wait for all jobs to settle — it waits for the stream to go quiet.

In the countdown test:
1. The mid-flight capture waits until count is between 1 and 9. Say it catches "8 running" — jobs 1-2 already done by then.
2. `await harness.waitForOutput(settleMs: 200)` — quick settle.
3. `drained = await harness.waitForOutput(settleMs: 500, timeout: 60s)` — waits for 2×500 ms of raw-buffer silence.

Now here's the race: jobs run `sleep 3..12`. Suppose mid-flight captured when 2 jobs had settled (8 running). Remaining 8 jobs settle at ~1 s intervals. Between settles there's ~1 s of silence — that's 2 consecutive 500 ms settles of stability → `waitForOutput` breaks EARLY, before the last jobs settle!

Wait, but the jobs settle ~1 s apart (sleep 3,4,...,12 staggered by 1 s each, started near-simultaneously). Between consecutive settle notices there's exactly ~1 s of quiet. `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500)`: after a notice lands, it needs 2 consecutive stable samples 500 ms apart to break — i.e., ~1 s of stability. If the next job settles exactly 1 s later, the buffer changes just as the loop is about to declare stability. It's a photo-finish: `stableTurns` reaches 2 only if two consecutive samples (500 ms apart) both saw no change. With notices arriving at ~1000 ms intervals, samples at t=500 (changed), t=1000 (changed — new notice), ... may never see 2 stable turns until the very end... but jitter could easily produce two stable samples mid-stream (e.g., two notices arrive close together then a 1.5 s gap, or the loop samples at 500/1000/1500 while notices arrive at 1050, 2050 → samples at 1500 and 2000 are stable → break).

That's exactly what happened on CI: `waitForOutput` returned after jobs 1–8 settled but before jobs 9 and 10 (the longest sleeps — they settle LAST, 11–12 s in, with the largest gap before them... wait no, gaps are all ~1 s).

Hmm wait, actually let's think again. Settle notices for jobs i at time T_start + (3+i) + ε roughly = 4, 5, 6, ..., 13 s. Between them ~1 s gaps. But the raw buffer also gets frame repaints (repaints re-emit notices, per the comment). Under CI load, repaints may pause.

The failure observed: settledNumbers = {1..8} — the drained capture cut off after 8 notices. Jobs 9, 10 settled at 12 and 13 s. The test had a 60 s timeout, so time wasn't the issue; the issue is `waitForOutput` returned early during a ≥1 silence window (which happens between EVERY pair of consecutive settles — the whole design "settles land ~1 s apart" makes 1 s quiet gaps guaranteed).

With settleMs: 500 and stableTurns >= 2: samples at 500 ms intervals; 2 stable turns = 1 s of no change. Notices ~1 s apart → the loop will often break right after a notice if the next one is >1 s away (CI jitter) or even at exactly ~1 s (samples at t+500 and t+1000; notice at t+1005 — stable! break).

So the test is inherently flaky by design: it uses a settle-window detector to await a process that continuously emits events every ~1 s. On a fast/quiet local machine the notice timing may be slightly less than 1 s apart so the loop keeps resetting; under CI load jitter stretches one inter-notice gap beyond ~1 s → premature return → missing notices 9, 10.

How to fix? Options:

A. Increase the settle window for the drained wait (settleMs larger, e.g. settleMs: 1500, requiring 3 s of silence — longer than any inter-notice gap) — but under heavy CI load, gaps could stretch past 3 s? The gaps are created by the job sleeps (staggered 1 s apart). Under load, notice DELIVERY could be delayed arbitrarily, but the sleeps still fire on wall-clock. If the PTY reader thread is starved, notices could bunch up (several arrive at once) followed by a long quiet — which would then break the loop early again with numbers missing? No — if they bunch up, they all arrive (in the buffer), and the quiet after them is genuinely the end. The risk is only a gap BETWEEN buffered notices that exceeds the stability window. Notices are written by the CLI to the PTY as jobs finish; under load, the CLI's event loop could be delayed, so notices for jobs finishing at 11 s and 12 s could be delivered at 14 s and 14.05 s (bunched), then quiet. In that case all notices eventually arrive; the early-break risk is when delivery gaps ≥ settle window occur BETWEEN notices that are both already finished but their writes are throttled. With settleMs 500, that's easy to hit. With a larger settle window, less likely but still possible in principle.

B. Anchor the wait: wait for `0 running` / the terminal summary instead of raw-output silence, then read the buffer. The test already does that AFTER the settledNumbers assertion: `waitForScreen('0 running', 30s)`. The correct fix: wait for the drained SCREEN first (`Background jobs (10) · 0 running · 10 done`), THEN collect the notices from the raw buffer. Reordering makes the assertion deterministic: the screen contract "10 done" guarantees all ten jobs settled; then the notices must be in the raw buffer.

Actually — wait. Is the assertion order the problem? Current order:
1. `drained = waitForOutput(settleMs: 500, timeout: 60)` — early-returns during a mid-drain silence gap.
2. Assert settledNumbers == {1..10} ← FAILS here (got {1..8}).
3. waitForScreen('0 running') etc.

The failure occurred at step 2 (test/integration/shell_job_countdown_pty_test.dart 157:7 — the settledNumbers expect). Line 157 is indeed the settledNumbers expect.

Fix approach (deterministic): after the mid-flight shot, wait for the drained screen (`0 running · 10 done`) with waitForScreen (anchored polling), then settle the raw output, THEN assert the distinct numbers from `drained` (the full raw buffer). This keeps the test's intent (every job started and finished) and removes the race: waitForScreen polls until the screen shows the final card, which only appears when all jobs are done.

Let me verify the sequence of what the final screen shows: 'Background jobs (10) · 0 running · 10 done · 0 lost'. The later assertion uses exactly that string. So:

```dart
// ── all ten FINISH: the drain is anchored on the terminal board ────
await harness.waitForScreen(
  'Background jobs (10) · 0 running · 10 done · 0 lost',
  timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
);
final drained = await harness.waitForOutput(settleMs: 500);
```

Then the settledNumbers assertion, then the rest (the existing `waitForScreen('0 running', 30)` + `waitForOutput(settleMs: 300)` + final asserts can stay, though now redundant — but keep minimal change: they're harmless).

Hmm wait, but there's a subtlety: does the final "Background jobs (10) · 0 running · 10 done · 0 lost" card appear on screen only after all 10 settle? Yes — `10 done` implies all ten finished. And settle notices are emitted into the raw stream as jobs finish (the board counts from them, presumably). Could a notice be MISSING from the raw buffer while the board still shows 10 done? The board's done-count derives from the same settle events. If the raw stream dropped a notice (fragmentation?), the board wouldn't count it... The comment in the test says frame repaints RE-EMIT notices into the raw stream, so repaints only add duplicates, not drops. The raw buffer accumulates monotonically (_rawBuffer is appended, never truncated — `waitForOutput` returns `_rawBuffer.toString()`).

But hold on — is it possible a settle notice appears on screen but never in the raw buffer? The raw buffer is the PTY output stream; the screen is a terminal emulator rendering of that same stream. Screen content always comes from the raw stream. So if the board shows 10 done, the notices were in the stream. # contract as play_upload_preflight.rb so the CI fastlane suites run it on
# the runner's stock ruby.
#

# appends screenshot uploads to the existing set, so whatever is stale on
# the listing (an old-copy screenshot, a device type or locale the repo no
# longer generates — ru-RU tenInch, for instance) survives the upload
# forever. Google reviewed that stale image and rejected the dev.fa1.app
# update on Sep 24 while the repo goldens were already fixed.
#
# This module replaces the WHOLE listing-image state per locale and device

#      read is retried with backoff, and an unreadable remote aborts with
#      its own "remote unreadable" class, never as a byte mismatch);
#   2. commit — a failed upload aborts BEFORE the commit, so the live
#      listing keeps its previous state;

require "digest"
require "json"
require "net/http"
require "openssl"
require "uri"

  UPLOAD_ROOT = "https://androidpublisher.googleapis.com/upload/androidpublisher/v3/applications"
  TOKEN_URL = "https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token"
  SCOPE = "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/androidpublisher"

  # Multi-slot types: Play APPENDS uploads, so every listing locale gets its
  # remote set cleared first — including types the repo no longer generates
  # (ru-RU tenInchScreenshots) and never generated (sevenInchScreenshots).
  SCREENSHOT_TYPES = %w[phoneScreenshots sevenInchScreenshots tenInchScreenshots].freeze
  # Single-slot types: an upload replaces the stored image by itself.
  SINGLE_IMAGE_TYPES = %w[icon featureGraphic].freeze
  # The image types this sync manages. validate_image_type! pins every
  # image call against this list BEFORE any HTTP request — it is a
  # module-local guard, NOT the full AppImageType enum (tvScreenshots,
  # wearScreenshots, promo graphics, …). EXTEND THIS LIST (in lock-step
  # with clear_plan/expected_state/sync_and_verify!) when adding managed
  # types, or the new types will be rejected pre-flight.
  MANAGED_TYPES = (SCREENSHOT_TYPES + SINGLE_IMAGE_TYPES).freeze

  module_function

  # ── pure helpers (unit-tested, no I/O beyond the metadata dir) ──────────

  # The locale dirs the repo ships (fastlane/metadata/android/<locale>/).
  def repo_locales(metadata_dir)
    Dir.children(metadata_dir)
       .select { |entry| File.directory?(File.join(metadata_dir, entry)) }
       .sort
  end

  # Committed golden paths for a locale/type, sorted (file name order IS
  # the Play listing order). Screenshot types live in an images/<type>/
  # dir; the single-slot types are flat files (images/icon.png,
  # images/featureGraphic.png). Missing everything = the repo ships none.
  def local_images(metadata_dir, locale, type)
    dir = File.join(metadata_dir, locale, "images", type)
    file = "#{dir}.png"
    paths =
      if Dir.exist?(dir)
        Dir.children(dir).grep(/\.png\z/i).sort.map { |name| File.join(dir, name) }
      elsif File.exist?(file)
        [file]
      else
        []
      end
    paths.sort
  end

  def sha256(path)
    Digest::SHA256.file(path).hexdigest
  end

  # The screenshot sets to clear: every listing locale (repo ∪ live on the
  # console) × every multi-slot type.
  def clear_plan(metadata_dir, remote_locales)
    all_locales(metadata_dir, remote_locales).flat_map do |locale|
      SCREENSHOT_TYPES.map { |type| { locale: locale, type: type } }
    end
  end

  # The post-sync state the listing must have: sha256 SEQUENCES per
  # [locale, type] in listing order (local_images sorts — file name order
  # IS the Play listing order) — the repo goldens where they exist, empty
  # where they do not (ru-RU tenInch, dropped locales).
  #
  # icon/featureGraphic are single-slot brand assets and Play Console does
  # not allow an empty icon on a listing locale, so for locales the repo
  # does NOT ship they are "don't care": a console-created locale keeps

  # screenshot sets there — issue #947 review).
  def expected_state(metadata_dir, remote_locales)
    repo = repo_locales(metadata_dir)
    all_locales(metadata_dir, remote_locales).to_h do |locale|
      types = repo.include?(locale) ? MANAGED_TYPES : SCREENSHOT_TYPES

        [type, local_images(metadata_dir, locale, type).map { |path| sha256(path) }]
      }]
    end
  end

  def all_locales(metadata_dir, remote_locales)

# CI runner's stock ruby), mirroring play_upload_preflight_test.rb:

#   ruby flutter_app/fastlane/test/play_listing_sync_test.rb
#
# Everything is exercised against a stateful fake of the androidpublisher
# REST transport — no network. The fake records every call so the checks
# pin the exact behaviour the Sep 24 rejection demanded: stale screenshot
# sets deleted per locale + device type (including ru-RU tenInch and
# never-generated sevenInch), goldens uploaded with sha256 verification,
# commit only after every image checks out, and a post-commit
# edits.images.list gate that fails on any drift.
#
# Guarded by $PROGRAM_NAME so an accidental require by fastlane's loader
# never executes the checks.

require "digest"
require "json"
require "openssl"
require "tmpdir"
require "fileutils"

require_relative "../play_listing_sync"

if $PROGRAM_NAME == __FILE__
  $checks = 0

  def ok(message)
    $checks += 1
    puts "  ok #{message}"
  end

  # ── fake transport ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Stateful androidpublisher stand-in: token → edit → listings →
  # delete/upload/list images → commit/delete-edit. The image paths mirror
  # the REAL androidpublisher v3 contract (gh-1261): the AppImageType enum
  # value sits DIRECTLY in the path (.../listings/<locale>/<imageType>) —
  # there is no "images" collection segment.
  class FakePlayHttp
    attr_reader :calls, :store, :committed
    attr_accessor :upload_sha_override, :upload_omit_sha, :token_response, :remote_languages,
                  :post_commit_drift, :post_commit_reverse, :image_delete_error,
                  :edit_insert_error, :listings_error, :commit_error,
                  :hide_shas_until_list_no

    def initialize
      @calls = []
      @store = Hash.new { |h, key| h[key] = [] }
      @committed = []
      @remote_languages = %w[en-US ru-RU]
      @list_reads = Hash.new(0)
    end

    def request(method, url, headers: {}, body: nil, content_type: nil)
      @calls << [method, url]
      case
      when method == :Post && url.include?("oauth2.googleapis.com/token")
        @token_assertion = body
        @token_response || { status: 200, body: { access_token: "[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]" }.to_json }
      when method == :Post && url.end_with?("/edits")
        return @edit_insert_error if @edit_insert_error
        { status: 200, body: { id: "edit1" }.to_json }
      when method == :Get && url.end_with?("/listings")
        return @listings_error if @listings_error
        { status: 200, body: { listings: @remote_languages.map { |l| { language: l } } }.to_json }
      when method == :Delete && (m = url.match(%r{/listings/([^/]+)/([^/]+)\z}))
        return @image_delete_error if @image_delete_error
        @store.delete([m[1], m[2]])
        { status: 204, body: "" }
      when method == :Post && (m = url.match(%r{/listings/([^/]+)/([^/]+)\?uploadType=media\z}))
        sha = @upload_sha_override || Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(body.to_s)
        @store[[m[1], m[2]]] << sha
        # gh-1328: Play sometimes 200s the upload WITHOUT a usable sha256
        # while the image is still processing.
        { status: 200, body: (@upload_omit_sha ? {} : { sha256: sha }).to_json }
      when method == :Get && (m = url.match(%r{/listings/([^/]+)/([^/]+)\z}))
        key = [m[1], m[2]]
        @list_reads[key] += 1
        images = @store[key].map { |s| { sha256: s } }
        # Post-commit drift injection: the committed listing keeps an image
        # the sync never uploaded (the stale-state failure mode #947 gates).
        if !@committed.empty? && @post_commit_drift == key
          images += [{ sha256: Digest::SHA256.hexdigest("drift-junk") }]
        end
        # Post-commit order injection: the committed listing serves the same
        # image set in a different order (the ordering failure mode).
        images.reverse! if !@committed.empty? && @post_commit_reverse == key
        # gh-1328: an entry (or its sha) may be unreadable until Play
        # finishes processing the just-uploaded bytes.
        images = images.map { |img| { sha256: nil } } if @hide_shas_until_list_no && @list_reads[key] <= @hide_shas_until_list_no
        { status: 200, body: { images: images }.to_json }
      when method == :Post && url.end_with?(":commit")
        return @commit_error if @commit_error
        @committed << url
        { status: 200, body: { id: "edit1" }.to_json }
      when method == :Delete && url.end_with?("/edits/edit1")
        { status: 200, body: "" }
      else
        raise "unexpected call: #{method} #{url}"
      end
    end
  end

  def write_png(path, bytes)
    FileUtils.mkdir_p(File.dirname(path))
    File.binwrite(path, bytes)
    path
  end

  def metadata_dir_with_goldens(root)
    # Mirrors the real tree shape: en-US carries icon + featureGraphic +
    # phone + tenInch sets; ru-RU has NO tenInch set (falls back to phone).
    base = File.join(root, "android")
    write_png(File.join(base, "en-US/images/icon.png"), "icon-en")
    write_png(File.join(base, "en-US/images/featureGraphic.png"), "fg-en")
    write_png(File.join(base, "en-US/images/phoneScreenshots/01_store_chat.png"), "phone-en-1")
    write_png(File.join(base, "en-US/images/phoneScreenshots/02_store_apps.png"), "phone-en-2")
    write_png(File.join(base, "en-US/images/tenInchScreenshots/01_store_chat.png"), "ten-en-1")
    write_png(File.join(base, "ru-RU/images/icon.png"), "icon-ru")
    write_png(File.join(base, "ru-RU/images/phoneScreenshots/01_store_chat.png"), "phone-ru-1")
    base
  end

  def service_account_json
    @key ||= OpenSSL::PKey::RSA.generate(2048)
    JSON.generate(
      "client_email" => "play@fa1.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
      "private_key" => @key.to_pem
    )
  end

  puts "play_listing_sync:"

  # ── pure helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Dir.mktmpdir do |root|
    metadata_dir = metadata_dir_with_goldens(root)

    locales = PlayListingSync.repo_locales(metadata_dir)
    raise "FAIL: repo locales #{locales.inspect}" unless locales == %w[en-US ru-RU]
    ok("repo locales discovered from the metadata dirs")

    phone = PlayListingSync.local_images(metadata_dir, "en-US", "phoneScreenshots")
    raise "FAIL: phone shots not sorted" unless phone.map { |p| File.basename(p) } == ["01_store_chat.png", "02_store_apps.png"]
    raise "FAIL: missing dir must yield []" unless PlayListingSync.local_images(metadata_dir, "ru-RU", "tenInchScreenshots") == []

    raise "FAIL: ru-RU tenInch expected EMPTY" unless state["ru-RU"]["tenInchScreenshots"] == []
    raise "FAIL: expected state must carry sha256 digests" unless state["en-US"]["icon"] == [Digest::SHA256.hexdigest("icon-en")]
    ok("expected state = repo goldens by sha256, empty where the repo ships none")
  end

    http = FakePlayHttp.new
    metadata_dir = metadata_dir_with_goldens(root)

Confirmed: the Fastfile call site uses defaults. Now let me start the TDD work.

## Plan

**Fix 1 — CI root cause (BLOCKING): flaky PTY countdown drain** (`test/integration/shell_job_countdown_pty_test.dart`)
- RED evidence: CI run 37555363161 harvested {1..8} of 10; same family as gh-1250 (run 37521987367, {1..5} of 10).
- Fix: anchor the drained harvest on the drained board row (gh-1250 precedent commit a2e4bfabf), test-only.

**Fix 2 — Thread 1: empty-string sha hardening** (`play_listing_sync.rb`)
- RED: new unit — upload answers `{sha256: ""}` → must poll → never `remote sha mismatch`; plus list-side `""` entries treated as unreadable.
- GREEN: `stored.to_s.strip.empty?` gate + list-read `.reject { |sha| sha.to_s.strip.empty? }`.

**Fix 3 — Thread 2: single-slot assumption documented** (comment only).

**Fix 4 — Thread 3: comment math** (comment only).

**Fix 5 — Thread 4: partial-out-of-order pin** (test only, pins existing conservative behavior — green on arrival).

Then run: ruby suite full; dart countdown test + reg guard; write outputs.

Order of operations per TDD: write the RED tests first, run them against the unfixed module, then fix, then run everything.

Let me write the RED tests for thread 1 first. In the test file, after the existing "nil stored sha is retried" block, add:

```ruby
# gh-1328 rework: an EMPTY-STRING sha is the same unreadable payload shape —
# `{"sha256": ""}` must route to the poll, never to the byte-mismatch class.
poll = PollHttp.new([[{ "sha256" => "" }],
                     [{ "sha256" => sha1 }]])
verified = PlayListingSync.poll_stored_sha!(...)
```

Hmm wait — the poll unit drives poll_stored_sha! directly; the empty-string gate lives in sync_and_verify!'s caller side. To RED-test the gate, drive sync_and_verify! end-to-end with a FakePlayHttp whose upload returns `{sha256: ""}` and whose list materializes later:

```ruby
# End-to-end: `{"sha256": ""}` from the upload is the same UNREADABLE
# payload shape as an omitted field — it must poll to a verdict, never
# reach the byte-mismatch class (gh-1328 rework: thread-1 hardening).
Dir.mktmpdir do |root|
  http = FakePlayHttp.new
  http.upload_sha_override = ""   # {"sha256": ""} — truthy key, unusable sha
  http.hide_shas_until_list_no = 1
  metadata_dir = metadata_dir_with_goldens(root)
  summary = PlayListingSync.sync_and_verify!(...)
  # must go green, not raise remote sha mismatch
end
```

Wait — careful with `upload_sha_override = ""`: `sha = @upload_sha_override || Digest...` — "" is truthy in ruby → sha = "". Then `@store[key] << ""` — the store now holds "" as the stored sha! Then the list read returns `[{sha256: ""}]` — with `hide_shas_until_list_no = 1`, the first read of each key maps everything to `{sha256: nil}`... but the poll's compact drops nil → readable=[] → retry; on read 2, entries serve their stored shas = "" → readable = [""] → `readable.any? { |sha| !expected_prefix.include?(sha) }` → "" not in expected → FALSE MISMATCH again via the list side! This confirms the list side ALSO needs the emptiness reject for the end-to-end to go green.

So with both fixes:
- upload gate: `stored.to_s.strip.empty?` → poll.
- poll list-read: `.map { sha256 }.reject { |s| s.to_s.strip.empty? }` — hmm wait, but then readable = [] on read 2 too (entry sha is ""). read 2..N always [] → never equals expected → returns nil → raise `remote unreadable after 5 attempts`. So end-to-end with override "" → unreadable abort (not mismatch). That's the honest classification: the fake stored "" as the actual sha, Play served "" consistently — genuinely unreadable.

For a GREEN end-to-end variant: upload `""` but the STORED sha is fine — that's contradictory (the fake stores what it returns). Better green case: upload omit-sha (nil) as today → green (already covered). For the empty-string case the correct expected behavior is: poll → unreadable class, never mismatch. So the end-to-end test asserts the `remote unreadable after N attempts` raise, message NOT containing "stored different bytes", no commit. And optionally, if the listing later materializes with the REAL sha — impossible in this fake since it stored "". Fine: pin the classification.

Also a poll-level unit for list-side "": readable [""] with expected [sha1] → must be treated as unreadable (retry → nil), not mismatch:

```ruby
poll = PollHttp.new([[{ "sha256" => "" }]] * 2)
verdict = poll_stored_sha!(... expected [sha1] ...) → nil (not raise)
```

RED on both today: today the upload "" never reaches poll (gate nil-only) → e2e raises `remote sha mismatch (sha256 "" != local …)` → test red. The poll-level "" test: readable [""] → `any?{!include?}` → mismatch raise → test red. 

Now the partial-out-of-order pin (thread 4) — green on arrival.

Message wording: the caller's unreadable raise says "Play never returned a usable sha256 for the just-uploaded image" — thread 4's nano-nit says slightly off for the partial case but "not worth chasing" — leave.

Also should the upload-gate change update the module header comment? The header says "a nil stored sha means Play is still processing" — extend to "a nil/empty stored sha". Cheap and accurate.

Now the comment fixes:

Thread 3: in poll_stored_sha! docstring: "(attempts × backoff seconds)" → "((attempts - 1) sleeps of `backoff` between `attempts` reads)".

Thread 2: add to poll_stored_sha! docstring (and/or the gh-1328 caller comment): the single-slot assumption — for icon/featureGraphic replaces, no clear runs first, so during the processing window the listing is expected to serve a nil entry (or the old sha is gone once replacement lands); if Play ever serves the PREVIOUS image's sha for a single-slot replace, the poll classifies a mismatch — deliberate per the issue's foreign-sha→mismatch table. Document.

Now the dart test fix. Current lines ~135-160:

```dart

      final drained = await harness.waitForOutput(
        settleMs: 500,
        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),

```

```dart

      // gh-1250 family ... (comment)
      await harness.waitForText(
        _drainedRow,
        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 90),
      );
      await harness.waitForOutput(settleMs: 300);
      final drained = harness.rawOutput;
```

And add the `_drainedRow` const, and use it in the final contains assertion (replacing the literal).

The final block currently:
```dart
      await harness.waitForScreen(
        '0 running',
        timeout: const Duration(seconds: 30),
      );
      await harness.waitForOutput(settleMs: 300);
      final after = harness.viewportLines;
      ...
      expect(screen, contains('Background jobs (10) · 0 running · 10 done · 0 lost'), ...)
```

messages.preview: The failing test uses `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500)` to await the drain — but settle notices arrive ~1 s apart **by design** (staggered sleeps 3–12 s), so any CI jitter stretching one gap past the ~1 …

blocks.text:
I see the bug pattern now. In `waitForOutput`:

```dart
while (DateTime.now().isBefore(deadline)) {
  await Future<void>.delayed(Duration(milliseconds: settleMs));
  if (_rawBuffer.length == lastLength) {
    if (++stableTurns >= 2) break;
  } else {
    ...
  }
```

`waitForOutput` returns as soon as the raw buffer is stable for 2 consecutive settles (500 ms each in the drained call = ~1 s of silence). It does NOT wait for all jobs to settle — it waits for the stream to go quiet.

In the countdown test:
1. The mid-flight capture waits until count is between 1 and 9. Say it catches "8 running" — jobs 1-2 already done by then.
2. `await harness.waitForOutput(settleMs: 200)` — quick settle.
3. `drained = await harness.waitForOutput(settleMs: 500, timeout: 60s)` — waits for 2×500 ms of raw-buffer silence.

Now here's the race: jobs run `sleep 3..12`. Suppose mid-flight captured when 2 jobs had settled (8 running). Remaining 8 jobs settle at ~1 s intervals. Between settles there's ~1 s of silence — that's 2 consecutive 500 ms settles of stability → `waitForOutput` breaks EARLY, before the last jobs settle!

Wait, but the jobs settle ~1 s apart (sleep 3,4,...,12 staggered by 1 s each, started near-simultaneously). Between consecutive settle notices there's exactly ~1 s of quiet. `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500)`: after a notice lands, it needs 2 consecutive stable samples 500 ms apart to break — i.e., ~1 s of stability. If the next job settles exactly 1 s later, the buffer changes just as the loop is about to declare stability. It's a photo-finish: `stableTurns` reaches 2 only if two consecutive samples (500 ms apart) both saw no change. With notices arriving at ~1000 ms intervals, samples at t=500 (changed), t=1000 (changed — new notice), ... may never see 2 stable turns until the very end... but jitter could easily produce two stable samples mid-stream (e.g., two notices arrive close together then a 1.5 s gap, or the loop samples at 500/1000/1500 while notices arrive at 1050, 2050 → samples at 1500 and 2000 are stable → break).

That's exactly what happened on CI: `waitForOutput` returned after jobs 1–8 settled but before jobs 9 and 10 (the longest sleeps — they settle LAST, 11–12 s in, with the largest gap before them... wait no, gaps are all ~1 s).

Hmm wait, actually let's think again. Settle notices for jobs i at time T_start + (3+i) + ε roughly = 4, 5, 6, ..., 13 s. Between them ~1 s gaps. But the raw buffer also gets frame repaints (repaints re-emit notices, per the comment). Under CI load, repaints may pause.

The failure observed: settledNumbers = {1..8} — the drained capture cut off after 8 notices. Jobs 9, 10 settled at 12 and 13 s. The test had a 60 s timeout, so time wasn't the issue; the issue is `waitForOutput` returned early during a ≥1 silence window (which happens between EVERY pair of consecutive settles — the whole design "settles land ~1 s apart" makes 1 s quiet gaps guaranteed).

With settleMs: 500 and stableTurns >= 2: samples at 500 ms intervals; 2 stable turns = 1 s of no change. Notices ~1 s apart → the loop will often break right after a notice if the next one is >1 s away (CI jitter) or even at exactly ~1 s (samples at t+500 and t+1000; notice at t+1005 — stable! break).

So the test is inherently flaky by design: it uses a settle-window detector to await a process that continuously emits events every ~1 s. On a fast/quiet local machine the notice timing may be slightly less than 1 s apart so the loop keeps resetting; under CI load jitter stretches one inter-notice gap beyond ~1 s → premature return → missing notices 9, 10.

How to fix? Options:

A. Increase the settle window for the drained wait (settleMs larger, e.g. settleMs: 1500, requiring 3 s of silence — longer than any inter-notice gap) — but under heavy CI load, gaps could stretch past 3 s? The gaps are created by the job sleeps (staggered 1 s apart). Under load, notice DELIVERY could be delayed arbitrarily, but the sleeps still fire on wall-clock. If the PTY reader thread is starved, notices could bunch up (several arrive at once) followed by a long quiet — which would then break the loop early again with numbers missing? No — if they bunch up, they all arrive (in the buffer), and the quiet after them is genuinely the end. The risk is only a gap BETWEEN buffered notices that exceeds the stability window. Notices are written by the CLI to the PTY as jobs finish; under load, the CLI's event loop could be delayed, so notices for jobs finishing at 11 s and 12 s could be delivered at 14 s and 14.05 s (bunched), then quiet. In that case all notices eventually arrive; the early-break risk is when delivery gaps ≥ settle window occur BETWEEN notices that are both already finished but their writes are throttled. With settleMs 500, that's easy to hit. With a larger settle window, less likely but still possible in principle.

B. Anchor the wait: wait for `0 running` / the terminal summary instead of raw-output silence, then read the buffer. The test already does that AFTER the settledNumbers assertion: `waitForScreen('0 running', 30s)`. The correct fix: wait for the drained SCREEN first (`Background jobs (10) · 0 running · 10 done`), THEN collect the notices from the raw buffer. Reordering makes the assertion deterministic: the screen contract "10 done" guarantees all ten jobs settled; then the notices must be in the raw buffer.

Actually — wait. Is the assertion order the problem? Current order:
1. `drained = waitForOutput(settleMs: 500, timeout: 60)` — early-returns during a mid-drain silence gap.
2. Assert settledNumbers == {1..10} ← FAILS here (got {1..8}).
3. waitForScreen('0 running') etc.

The failure occurred at step 2 (test/integration/shell_job_countdown_pty_test.dart 157:7 — the settledNumbers expect). Line 157 is indeed the settledNumbers expect.

Fix approach (deterministic): after the mid-flight shot, wait for the drained screen (`0 running · 10 done`) with waitForScreen (anchored polling), then settle the raw output, THEN assert the distinct numbers from `drained` (the full raw buffer). This keeps the test's intent (every job started and finished) and removes the race: waitForScreen polls until the screen shows the final card, which only appears when all jobs are done.

Let me verify the sequence of what the final screen shows: 'Background jobs (10) · 0 running · 10 done · 0 lost'. The later assertion uses exactly that string. So:

```dart
// ── all ten FINISH: the drain is anchored on the terminal board ────
await harness.waitForScreen(
  'Background jobs (10) · 0 running · 10 done · 0 lost',
  timeout: const Duration(seconds: 60),
);
final drained = await harness.waitForOutput(settleMs: 500);
```

Then the settledNumbers assertion, then the rest (the existing `waitForScreen('0 running', 30)` + `waitForOutput(settleMs: 300)` + final asserts can stay, though now redundant — but keep minimal change: they're harmless).

Hmm wait, but there's a subtlety: does the final "Background jobs (10) · 0 running · 10 done · 0 lost" card appear on screen only after all 10 settle? Yes — `10 done` implies all ten finished. And settle notices are emitted into the raw stream as jobs finish (the board counts from them, presumably). Could a notice be MISSING from the raw buffer while the board still shows 10 done? The board's done-count derives from the same settle events. If the raw stream dropped a notice (fragmentation?), the board wouldn't count it... The comment in the test says frame repaints RE-EMIT notices into the raw stream, so repaints only add duplicates, not drops. The raw buffer accumulates monotonically (_rawBuffer is appended, never truncated — `waitForOutput` returns `_rawBuffer.toString()`).

But hold on — is it possible a settle notice appears on screen but never in the raw buffer? The raw buffer is the PTY output stream; the screen is a terminal emulator rendering of that same stream. Screen content always comes from the raw stream. So if the board shows 10 done, the notices were in the stream. A notice could be split by interleaved escapes (hence the number-prefix matching), but the set-based assertion handles that (already in place).

Also the possibi…

The failing test uses `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500)` to await the drain — but settle notices arrive ~1 s apart **by design** (staggered sleeps 3–12 s), so any CI jitter stretching one gap past the ~1 s stability window returns early with notices 9/10 missing. Let me confirm the flake history before fixing.

# frozen_string_literal: true

# Play listing-image sync (issue #947). Plain ruby, no gems — the same
# contract as play_upload_preflight.rb so the CI fastlane suites run it on
# the runner's stock ruby.
#
# Why this exists: the supply `play_store` lane only UPLOADS images. Play
# appends screenshot uploads to the existing set, so whatever is stale on
# the listing (an old-copy screenshot, a device type or locale the repo no
# longer generates — ru-RU tenInch, for instance) survives the upload
# forever. Google reviewed that stale image and rejected the dev.fa1.app
# update on Sep 24 while the repo goldens were already fixed.
#
# This module replaces the WHOLE listing-image state per locale and device
# type, then proves the committed state matches the repo goldens:
#
#   1. one edit: clear every managed screenshot set for EVERY listing
#      locale (repo locales ∪ locales live on the Play listing), then
#      upload the committed goldens (sorted — file name order is the
#      listing order), checking each stored sha256 against the local file
#      (gh-1328: a nil stored sha means Play is still processing — the
#      read is retried with backoff, and an unreadable remote aborts with
#      its own "remote unreadable" class, never as a byte mismatch);
#   2. commit — a failed upload aborts BEFORE the commit, so the live
#      listing keeps its previous state;
#   3. a fresh read-only edit re-reads edits.images.list and fails the job
#      unless every managed locale/type matches the goldens exactly
#      (icon + featureGraphic + all screenshot types, empty where the repo
#      ships nothing).
#
# supply keeps handling the metadata TEXTS (the lane passes
# skip_upload_images/skip_upload_screenshots); images ride this module only.
require "base64"
require "digest"
require "json"
require "net/http"
require "openssl"
require "uri"

module PlayListingSync
  API_ROOT = "https://androidpublisher.googleapis.com/androidpublisher/v3/applications"
  # Media-upload host prefix: edits.images.upload POSTs the SAME path under
  # the /upload/ prefix with ?uploadType=media (gh-1261).
  UPLOAD_ROOT = "https://androidpublisher.googleapis.com/upload/androidpublisher/v3/applications"
  TOKEN_URL = "https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token"
  SCOPE = "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/androidpublisher"

  # Multi-slot types: Play APPENDS uploads, so every listing locale gets its
  # remote set cleared first — including types the repo no longer generates
  # (ru-RU tenInchScreenshots) and never generated (sevenInchScreenshots).
  SCREENSHOT_TYPES = %w[phoneScreenshots sevenInchScreenshots tenInchScreenshots].freeze
  # Single-slot types: an upload replaces the stored image by itself.
  SINGLE_IMAGE_TYPES = %w[icon featureGraphic].freeze
  # The image types this sync manages. validate_image_type! pins every
  # image call against this list BEFORE any HTTP request — it is a
  # module-local guard, NOT the full AppImageType enum (tvScreenshots,
  # wearScreenshots, promo graphics, …). EXTEND THIS LIST (in lock-step
  # with clear_plan/expected_state/sync_and_verify!) when adding managed
  # types, or the new types will be rejected pre-flight.
  MANAGED_TYPES = (SCREENSHOT_TYPES + SINGLE_IMAGE_TYPES).freeze

  module_function

  # ── pure helpers (unit-tested, no I/O beyond the metadata dir) ──────────

  # The locale dirs the repo ships (fastlane/metadata/android/<locale>/).
  def repo_locales(metadata_dir)
    Dir.children(metadata_dir)
       .select { |entry| File.directory?(File.join(metadata_dir, entry)) }
       .sort
  end

  # Committed golden paths for a locale/type, sorted (file name order IS
  # the Play listing order). Screenshot types live in an images/<type>/
  # dir; the single-slot types are flat files (images/icon.png,
  # images/featureGraphic.png). Missing everything = the repo ships none.
  def local_images(metadata_dir, locale, type)
    dir = File.join(metadata_dir, locale, "images", type)
    file = "#{dir}.png"
    paths =
      if Dir.exist?(dir)
        Dir.children(dir).grep(/\.png\z/i).sort.map { |name| File.join(dir, name) }
      elsif File.exist?(file)
        [file]
      else
        []
      end
    paths.sort
  end

  def sha256(path)
    Digest::SHA256.file(path).hexdigest
  end

  # The screenshot sets to clear: every listing locale (repo ∪ live on the
  # console) × every multi-slot type.
  def clear_plan(metadata_dir, remote_locales)
    all_locales(metadata_dir, remote_locales).flat_map do |locale|
      SCREENSHOT_TYPES.map { |type| { locale: locale, type: type } }
    end
  end

  # The post-sync state the listing must have: sha256 SEQUENCES per
  # [locale, type] in listing order (local_images sorts — file name order
  # IS the Play listing order) — the repo goldens where they exist, empty
  # where they do not (ru-RU tenInch, dropped locales).
  #
  # icon/featureGraphic are single-slot brand assets and Play Console does
  # not allow an empty icon on a listing locale, so for locales the repo
  # does NOT ship they are "don't care": a console-created locale keeps
  # its icon/feature graphic (the sync only clears + enforces the
  # screenshot sets there — issue #947 review).
  def expected_state(metadata_dir, remote_locales)
    repo = repo_locales(metadata_dir)
    all_locales(metadata_dir, remote_locales).to_h do |locale|
      types = repo.include?(locale) ? MANAGED_TYPES : SCREENSHOT_TYPES
      [locale, types.to_h { |type|
        [type, local_images(metadata_dir, locale, type).map { |path| sha256(path) }]
      }]
    end
  end

  def all_locales(metadata_dir, remote_locales)

#   ruby flutter_app/fastlane/test/play_listing_sync_test.rb
#
# Everything is exercised against a stateful fake of the androidpublisher
# REST transport — no network. The fake records every call so the checks
# pin the exact behaviour the Sep 24 rejection demanded: stale screenshot
# sets deleted per locale + device type (including ru-RU tenInch and
# never-generated sevenInch), goldens uploaded with sha256 verification,
# commit only after every image checks out, and a post-commit
# edits.images.list gate that fails on any drift.
#
# Guarded by $PROGRAM_NAME so an accidental require by fastlane's loader
# never executes the checks.

require "digest"
require "json"
require "openssl"
require "tmpdir"
require "fileutils"

require_relative "../play_listing_sync"

if $PROGRAM_NAME == __FILE__
  $checks = 0

  def ok(message)
    $checks += 1
    puts "  ok #{message}"
  end

  # Stateful androidpublisher stand-in: token → edit → listings →
  # delete/upload/list images → commit/delete-edit. The image paths mirror
  # the REAL androidpublisher v3 contract (gh-1261): the AppImageType enum
  # value sits DIRECTLY in the path (.../listings/<locale>/<imageType>) —
  # there is no "images" collection segment.
  class FakePlayHttp
    attr_reader :calls, :store, :committed
    attr_accessor :upload_sha_override, :upload_omit_sha, :token_response, :remote_languages,
                  :post_commit_drift, :post_commit_reverse, :image_delete_error,
                  :edit_insert_error, :listings_error, :commit_error,
                  :hide_shas_until_list_no

    def initialize
      @calls = []
      @store = Hash.new { |h, key| h[key] = [] }
      @committed = []
      @remote_languages = %w[en-US ru-RU]
      @list_reads = Hash.new(0)
    end

    def request(method, url, headers: {}, body: nil, content_type: nil)
      @calls << [method, url]
      case

        @token_assertion = body
        @token_response || { status: 200, body: { access_token: "[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]" }.to_json }
      when method == :Post && url.end_with?("/edits")
        return @edit_insert_error if @edit_insert_error
        { status: 200, body: { id: "edit1" }.to_json }
      when method == :Get && url.end_with?("/listings")
        return @listings_error if @listings_error
        { status: 200, body: { listings: @remote_languages.map { |l| { language: l } } }.to_json }
      when method == :Delete && (m = url.match(%r{/listings/([^/]+)/([^/]+)\z}))
        return @image_delete_error if @image_delete_error
        @store.delete([m[1], m[2]])
        { status: 204, body: "" }
      when method == :Post && (m = url.match(%r{/listings/([^/]+)/([^/]+)\?uploadType=media\z}))
        sha = @upload_sha_override || Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(body.to_s)
        @store[[m[1], m[2]]] << sha
        # gh-1328: Play sometimes 200s the upload WITHOUT a usable sha256
        # while the image is still processing.
        { status: 200, body: (@upload_omit_sha ? {} : { sha256: sha }).to_json }
      when method == :Get && (m = url.match(%r{/listings/([^/]+)/([^/]+)\z}))
        key = [m[1], m[2]]
        @list_reads[key] += 1
        images = @store[key].map { |s| { sha256: s } }
        # Post-commit drift injection: the committed listing keeps an image
        # the sync never uploaded (the stale-state failure mode #947 gates).
        if !@committed.empty? && @post_commit_drift == key
          images += [{ sha256: Digest::SHA256.hexdigest("drift-junk") }]
        end
        # Post-commit order injection: the committed listing serves the same
        # image set in a different order (the ordering failure mode).
        images.reverse! if !@committed.empty? && @post_commit_reverse == key

        # finishes processing the just-uploaded bytes.
        images = images.map { |img| { sha256: nil } } if @hide_shas_until_list_no && @list_reads[key] <= @hide_shas_until_list_no

      when method == :Post && url.end_with?(":commit")

        @committed << url
        { status: 200, body: { id: "edit1" }.to_json }
      when method == :Delete && url.end_with?("/edits/edit1")
        { status: 200, body: "" }
      else
        raise "unexpected call: #{method} #{url}"
      end
    end
  end

  #   goldens (a real byte/ordering mismatch);
  #   returns nil when still unreadable after `attempts` — the caller
  #   aborts with the distinct "remote unreadable" class.
  #
  # Assumption (gh-1328 review): multi-slot sets are cleared first, so
  # during the processing window their list can only hold missing entries
  # or nil/blank shas — both retry. Single-slot types (icon/featureGraphic)
  # are NOT cleared (console-only locales keep theirs), so the poll relies
  # on Play serving a nil/blank entry — not the PREVIOUS image's sha —
  # while a replacement processes. A readable set contradicting the goldens
  # still classifies "remote sha mismatch" by design (the issue's
  # foreign-sha → mismatch table); if a daily leg ever reds on a single-slot
  # replace serving the old sha, treat that as unreadable here.
  def poll_stored_sha!(http, package_name, edit_id, locale, type, expected_prefix, auth,
                       attempts: 5, backoff: 30)

# Play listing-image sync (issue #947). Plain ruby, no gems — the same
# contract as play_upload_preflight.rb so the CI fastlane suites run it on
# the runner's stock ruby.
#
# Why this exists: the supply `play_store` lane only UPLOADS images. Play
# appends screenshot uploads to the existing set, so whatever is stale on
# the listing (an old-copy screenshot, a device type or locale the repo no
# longer generates — ru-RU tenInch, for instance) survives the upload
# forever. Google reviewed that stale image and rejected the dev.fa1.app
# update on Sep 24 while the repo goldens were already fixed.
#
# This module replaces the WHOLE listing-image state per locale and device
# type, then proves the committed state matches the repo goldens:

#   1. one edit: clear every managed screenshot set for EVERY listing

#      upload the committed goldens (sorted — file name order is the
#      listing order), checking each stored sha256 against the local file

#      read is retried with backoff, and an unreadable remote aborts with
#      its own "remote unreadable" class, never as a byte mismatch);
#   2. commit — a failed upload aborts BEFORE the commit, so the live
#      listing keeps its previous state;
#   3. a fresh read-only edit re-reads edits.images.list and fails the job
#      unless every managed locale/type matches the goldens exactly

#      ships nothing).

require "base64"
require "digest"
require "json"
require "net/http"
require "openssl"
require "uri"

  API_ROOT = "https://androidpublisher.googleapis.com/androidpublisher/v3/applications"
  # Media-upload host prefix: edits.images.upload POSTs the SAME path under
  # the /upload/ prefix with ?uploadType=media (gh-1261).
  UPLOAD_ROOT = "https://androidpublisher.googleapis.com/upload/androidpublisher/v3/applications"
  TOKEN_URL = "https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token"
  SCOPE = "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/androidpublisher"

  # Multi-slot types: Play APPENDS uploads, so every listing locale gets its
  # remote set cleared first — including types the repo no longer generates
  # (ru-RU tenInchScreenshots) and never generated (sevenInchScreenshots).
  SCREENSHOT_TYPES = %w[phoneScreenshots sevenInchScreenshots tenInchScreenshots].freeze
  # Single-slot types: an upload replaces the stored image by itself.
  SINGLE_IMAGE_TYPES = %w[icon featureGraphic].freeze
  # The image types this sync manages. validate_image_type! pins every
  # image call against this list BEFORE any HTTP request — it is a
  # module-local guard, NOT the full AppImageType enum (tvScreenshots,
  # wearScreenshots, promo graphics, …). EXTEND THIS LIST (in lock-step
  # with clear_plan/expected_state/sync_and_verify!) when adding managed
  # types, or the new types will be rejected pre-flight.
  MANAGED_TYPES = (SCREENSHOT_TYPES + SINGLE_IMAGE_TYPES).freeze

  module_function

  # ── pure helpers (unit-tested, no I/O beyond the metadata dir) ──────────

  # The locale dirs the repo ships (fastlane/metadata/android/<locale>/).
  def repo_locales(metadata_dir)
    Dir.children(metadata_dir)
       .select { |entry| File.directory?(File.join(metadata_dir, entry)) }
       .sort
  end

  # Committed golden paths for a locale/type, sorted (file name order IS
  # the Play listing order). Screenshot types live in an images/<type>/
  # dir; the single-slot types are flat files (images/icon.png,
  # images/featureGraphic.png). Missing everything = the repo ships none.
  def local_images(metadata_dir, locale, type)
    dir = File.join(metadata_dir, locale, "images", type)
    file = "#{dir}.png"
    paths =
      if Dir.exist?(dir)
        Dir.children(dir).grep(/\.png\z/i).sort.map { |name| File.join(dir, name) }
      elsif File.exist?(file)
        [file]
      else
        []
      end
    paths.sort
  end

  def sha256(path)
    Digest::SHA256.file(path).hexdigest
  end

  # The screenshot sets to clear: every listing locale (repo ∪ live on the
  # console) × every multi-slot type.
  def clear_plan(metadata_dir, remote_locales)
    all_locales(metadata_dir, remote_locales).flat_map do |locale|
      SCREENSHOT_TYPES.map { |type| { locale: locale, type: type } }
    end
  end

  # The post-sync state the listing must have: sha256 SEQUENCES per
  # [locale, type] in listing order (local_images sorts — file name order
  # IS the Play listing order) — the repo goldens where they exist, empty
  # where they do not (ru-RU tenInch, dropped locales).
  #
  # icon/featureGraphic are single-slot brand assets and Play Console does
  # not allow an empty icon on a listing locale, so for locales the repo
  # does NOT ship they are "don't care": a console-created locale keeps
  # its icon/feature graphic (the sync only clears + enforces the
  # screenshot sets there — issue #947 review).
  def expected_state(metadata_dir, remote_locales)
    repo = repo_locales(metadata_dir)
    all_locales(metadata_dir, remote_locales).to_h do |locale|
      types = repo.include?(locale) ? MANAGED_TYPES : SCREENSHOT_TYPES
      [locale, types.to_h { |type|
        [type, local_images(metadata_dir, locale, type).map { |path| sha256(path) }]
      }]
    end
  end

  def all_locales(metadata_dir, remote_locales)

  end

# Issue #947 — Play listing-image sync. Plain ruby, no gems (runs on the
# CI runner's stock ruby), mirroring play_upload_preflight_test.rb:
#
#   ruby flutter_app/fastlane/test/play_listing_sync_test.rb
#
# Everything is exercised against a stateful fake of the androidpublisher
# REST transport — no network. The fake records every call so the checks
# pin the exact behaviour the Sep 24 rejection demanded: stale screenshot
# sets deleted per locale + device type (including ru-RU tenInch and
# never-generated sevenInch), goldens uploaded with sha256 verification,
# commit only after every image checks out, and a post-commit
# edits.images.list gate that fails on any drift.
#
# Guarded by $PROGRAM_NAME so an accidental require by fastlane's loader
# never executes the checks.

require "digest"
require "json"
require "openssl"
require "tmpdir"
require "fileutils"

require_relative "../play_listing_sync"

if $PROGRAM_NAME == __FILE__
  $checks = 0

  def ok(message)
    $checks += 1
    puts "  ok #{message}"
  end

  # ── fake transport ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Stateful androidpublisher stand-in: token → edit → listings →
  # delete/upload/list images → commit/delete-edit. The image paths mirror
  # the REAL androidpublisher v3 contract (gh-1261): the AppImageType enum
  # value sits DIRECTLY in the path (.../listings/<locale>/<imageType>) —
  # there is no "images" collection segment.
  class FakePlayHttp
    attr_reader :calls, :store, :committed
    attr_accessor :upload_sha_override, :upload_omit_sha, :token_response, :remote_languages,
                  :post_commit_drift, :post_commit_reverse, :image_delete_error,
                  :edit_insert_error, :listings_error, :commit_error,
                  :hide_shas_until_list_no

    def initialize
      @calls = []
      @store = Hash.new { |h, key| h[key] = [] }
      @committed = []
      @remote_languages = %w[en-US ru-RU]
      @list_reads = Hash.new(0)
    end

    def request(method, url, headers: {}, body: nil, content_type: nil)
      @calls << [method, url]
      case
      when method == :Post && url.include?("oauth2.googleapis.com/token")
        @token_assertion = body
        @token_response || { status: 200, body: { access_token: "[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]" }.to_json }
      when method == :Post && url.end_with?("/edits")
        return @edit_insert_error if @edit_insert_error
        { status: 200, body: { id: "edit1" }.to_json }
      when method == :Get && url.end_with?("/listings")
        return @listings_error if @listings_error
        { status: 200, body: { listings: @remote_languages.map { |l| { language: l } } }.to_json }
      when method == :Delete && (m = url.match(%r{/listings/([^/]+)/([^/]+)\z}))
        return @image_delete_error if @image_delete_error
        @store.delete([m[1], m[2]])
        { status: 204, body: "" }
      when method == :Post && (m = url.match(%r{/listings/([^/]+)/([^/]+)\?uploadType=media\z}))
        sha = @upload_sha_override || Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(body.to_s)
        @store[[m[1], m[2]]] << sha
        # gh-1328: Play sometimes 200s the upload WITHOUT a usable sha256
        # while the image is still processing.
        { status: 200, body: (@upload_omit_sha ? {} : { sha256: sha }).to_json }
      when method == :Get && (m = url.match(%r{/listings/([^/]+)/([^/]+)\z}))
        key = [m[1], m[2]]
        @list_reads[key] += 1
        images = @store[key].map { |s| { sha256: s } }
        # Post-commit drift injection: the committed listing keeps an image
        # the sync never uploaded (the stale-state failure mode #947 gates).
        if !@committed.empty? && @post_commit_drift == key
          images += [{ sha256: Digest::SHA256.hexdigest("drift-junk") }]
        end
        # Post-commit order injection: the committed listing serves the same
        # image set in a different order (the ordering failure mode).
        images.reverse! if !@committed.empty? && @post_commit_reverse == key
        # gh-1328: an entry (or its sha) may be unreadable until Play
        # finishes processing the just-uploaded bytes.
        images = images.map { |img| { sha256: nil } } if @hide_shas_until_list_no && @list_reads[key] <= @hide_shas_until_list_no
        { status: 200, body: { images: images }.to_json }
      when method == :Post && url.end_with?(":commit")
        return @commit_error if @commit_error
        @committed << url
        { status: 200, body: { id: "edit1" }.to_json }
      when method == :Delete && url.end_with?("/edits/edit1")
        { status: 200, body: "" }
      else
        raise "unexpected call: #{method} #{url}"
      end
    end
  end

  def write_png(path, bytes)
    FileUtils.mkdir_p(File.dirname(path))
    File.binwrite(path, bytes)
    path
  end

  def metadata_dir_with_goldens(root)
    # Mirrors the real tree shape: en-US carries icon + featureGraphic +
    # phone + tenInch sets; ru-RU has NO tenInch set (falls back to phone).
    base = File.join(root, "android")
    write_png(File.join(base, "en-US/images/icon.png"), "icon-en")
    write_png(File.join(base, "en-US/images/featureGraphic.png"), "fg-en")
    write_png(File.join(base, "en-US/images/phoneScreenshots/01_store_chat.png"), "phone-en-1")
    write_png(File.join(base, "en-US/images/phoneScreenshots/02_store_apps.png"), "phone-en-2")
    write_png(File.join(base, "en-US/images/tenInchScreenshots/01_store_chat.png"), "ten-en-1")
    write_png(File.join(base, "ru-RU/images/icon.png"), "icon-ru")
    write_png(File.join(base, "ru-RU/images/phoneScreenshots/01_store_chat.png"), "phone-ru-1")
    base
  end

  def service_account_json
    @key ||= OpenSSL::PKey::RSA.generate(2048)
    JSON.generate(
      "client_email" => "play@fa1.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
      "private_key" => @key.to_pem
    )
  end

  puts "play_listing_sync:"

  # ── pure helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Dir.mktmpdir do |root|
    metadata_dir = metadata_dir_with_goldens(root)

    locales = PlayListingSync.repo_locales(metadata_dir)
    raise "FAIL: repo locales #{locales.inspect}" unless locales == %w[en-US ru-RU]
    ok("repo locales discovered from the metadata dirs")

    phone = PlayListingSync.local_images(metadata_dir, "en-US", "phoneScreenshots")
    raise "FAIL: phone shots not sorted" unless phone.map { |p| File.basename(p) } == ["01_store_chat.png", "02_store_apps.png"]
    raise "FAIL: missing dir must yield []" unless PlayListingSync.local_images(metadata_dir, "ru-RU", "tenInchScreenshots") == []
    ok("local image sets sorted; missing dirs yield an empty set")

    # and sevenInch (never generated).
    plan = PlayListingSync.clear_plan(metadata_dir, ["de-DE"])
    expected = %w[de-DE en-US ru-RU].product(PlayListingSync::SCREENSHOT_TYPES).size
    raise "FAIL: clear plan size #{plan.size} != #{expected}" unless plan.size == expected
    raise "FAIL: ru-RU tenInch must be cleared" unless plan.any? { |e| e[:locale] == "ru-RU" && e[:type] == "tenInchScreenshots" }
    raise "FAIL: console-only locale must be cleared" unless plan.any? { |e| e[:locale] == "de-DE" }
    ok("clear plan = every listing locale × every multi-slot type (#{expected} sets)")

    state = PlayListingSync.expected_state(metadata_dir, [])
    raise "FAIL: en-US tenInch expected non-empty" unless state["en-US"]["tenInchScreenshots"].size == 1
    raise "FAIL: ru-RU tenInch expected EMPTY" unless state["ru-RU"]["tenInchScreenshots"] == []
    raise "FAIL: expected state must carry sha256 digests" unless state["en-US"]["icon"] == [Digest::SHA256.hexdigest("icon-en")]
    ok("expected state = repo goldens by sha256, empty where the repo ships none")
  end

  # ── service-account JWT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Dir.mktmpdir do |root|
    http = FakePlayHttp.new
    metadata_dir = metadata_dir_with_goldens(root)
    key = OpenSSL::PKey::RSA.generate(2048)
    json_key = JSON.generate("client_email" => "play@fa1.iam.gserviceacc…
